claims.text: The low-mixing-entropy TaNb-based baseline has a relatively homogeneous local lattice structure.
The low-mixing-entropy TaNb-based baseline has a relatively homogeneous superconducting-gap distribution.
Adding principal elements or changing their relative ratios can systematically increase configurational entropy in the TaNb-based alloy.
Increasing configurational entropy produces greater local lattice distortions.
Greater local lattice distortions modulate the local electron-phonon coupling strength.
Changes in electron-phonon coupling alter superconducting pairing interactions and gap magnitude.
Entropy-induced local lattice distortions consequently produce spatial fluctuations in the superconducting gap.
Higher-mixing-entropy samples will have a broader and more heterogeneous distribution of superconducting-gap values than the low-entropy baseline.
Higher-mixing-entropy samples will exhibit altered electron-phonon-coupling indicators relative to the low-entropy baseline.
Local regions with stronger lattice distortions will correlate with different superconducting-gap magnitudes.
The lower-entropy baseline may be produced using fewer elements.
The lower-entropy baseline may be produced using more equiatomic elements.
Weak disorder effects in the baseline are consistent with a relatively uniform superconducting-gap distribution.
The proposed mechanism is applicable to bcc-structured TaNb-based high-entropy alloys.
TaNb-based high-entropy alloy superconductivity can occur in the weak electron-phonon-coupling limit.
The distortion-mediated mechanism is expected to operate near the superconducting transition and without extreme pressure.
Specific elemental interactions may also influence superconducting properties.
A statistically significant increase in both spatial gap variability and corresponding electron-phonon-coupling changes is the decisive predicted outcome.

contradictions.description: The intervention proposes increasing configurational entropy by changing ratios toward higher mixing, whereas the baseline description lists 'more equiatomic elements' as a route to lower entropy. For a fixed element set, moving toward equiatomic ratios generally increases rather than decreases configurational entropy.
